title: Uniform secular-bath fidelity bound with specified affine applicability
statement: Under the stated nonresonance and uniform-rate premises, every one-qubit encoder and final decoder obey F_ent(t)<=(1+exp(-Ngt))/2. Nonzero-frequency jumps are rank one; local Pauli variance and the 12J^2 second moment give loss R>=NgI. All branches containing such a jump are entanglement breaking. A homogeneous gap-discriminant and a spanning-path witness establish nonresonance for almost every arbitrarily weak allowed affine perturbation of any fixed H0.

requires: Service: bounded-degree conflict graph, clean compatible ownership/tag states, continuously eligible requests and independent fixed-rate local CP-event proposal clocks. Bath: N qubits, simple spectrum and distinct ordered nonzero gaps, sup_i sum_{X contains i}||h_X||<=J, independent onsite X/Y/Z baths and all rates>=g>0 on |omega|<=4J uniformly in N. Affine genericity requires perturbation directions containing onsite X,Z and ZZ along one spanning nearest-neighbor path; uniform Jbar and g must persist. The other two results use the separately stated commuting-Pauli or two-qubit model.

assumptions: Exact fully secular generator time only. Resolving shrinking splittings can require size-dependent microscopic coupling and vanishing physical g_N. No fixed-coupling physical no-go, arbitrary restricted-support genericity or contradiction of quasi-local stationary-Gibbs memory theorems follows.
costs: For error epsilon<1/2, t<=-log(1-2epsilon)/(Ng). Affine coefficient boxes require uniform Jbar and positive rates on [-4Jbar,4Jbar]. Spectral-genericity and frequency-block machinery are credited predecessors.
